title: The dispatch of the demand, the addressee set, the approved template and the notice period are not specified for rwb-guarantee
source: Legacy RWB-E4-017 (04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md lines 3152 to 3232); FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3 A1.3, A2.5.2, A2.5.3.1 and A2.5.4; TSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v2 T3.1, T4, T5.1 and T5.3; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 row R-GUA-06; Context pack S3 (service row, ownership rows, slide 13 row S3); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01, DP-05, DP-09 and R7.2 s12
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow steps 4 to 9; 5 Exception paths X5 and X6; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1; 8 Business rules BR3 to BR6; 11 Data; 12.3; 12.5; 12.8; 13 Solution plan; 15 Screens and states
description: One combined row for the notice cycle of rwb-guarantee. (1) No source fixes how the demand reaches rwb-comms. FSD S3 v3 A2.5.2 names 'WIN, Workbench' as the integration points with no contract, no template set and no channel; Architecture v5 slide 13 draws T and E from S3 to P6 and no R, and the Ownership Map gives S3 zero published events, so neither a REST contract nor a service event is available and no source states which of the two the target uses. (2) No source states the addressee set or how the parties are obtained. The legacy data table names case_party, recovery_case and v_ace_customer, all owned by rwb-case and rwb-source-data under DP-01 and DP-05, and no source says which party role makes an addressee beyond the three values R-GUA-06 names in its condition. (3) No source states the template rule for a guarantee notice. FSD S3 A2.5.2 says only 'from the approved template', R-GUA-06 says 'issue the D6.6 guarantor notice with proof of delivery' and names WIN and DMS, and no document lists the notice types, the template codes, the rule that decides what is current or the reason codes of a refusal. (4) No source gives the notice period a home. The routing workbook carries 'Notice period by product' in its service-level column only, no parameter key is defined, and TSD S3 T3.1 gives guarantee_claim eight fields of which none is a notice date, a template code, an addressee or a dispatch reference, so the notice cannot be stored on the row the legacy story's data section names. (5) No source gives the notice a screen state. SCR-17 carries five states (Not due; due; submitted; paid; refused) and the stage vocabulary R-GUA-06 moves to, GUARANTOR_NOTICE, is not one of them, so the mapping is undefined. (6) The legacy endpoint table lists the claim create and the claim update only, so no source states on which operation the notice is recorded.
evidence: FSD S3 v3 A2.5.2 ('Integration points. WIN, Workbench'; 'Sends the demand to every guarantor and co-borrower on the case, from the approved template') and A2.5.3.1 (only VR-S3-005-1 and BR-S3-005) and A2.5.3.3 ('None; runs unattended'); TSD S3 v2 T3.1 (guarantee_claim, DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-022, no notice field) and T5.1 (INT-29 only) and T5.3 ('None'); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 row R-GUA-06 ('Issue the D6.6 guarantor notice with proof of delivery | GUARANTOR_NOTICE | Guarantor | WIN and DMS, Workbench | Notice period by product'); Context pack S3 Ownership rows ('Events (0)', tables 'guarantee_claim', operations PATCH and POST only) and slide 13 row 'S3 Guarantee | P7 T | P6 T E | P8 E'; legacy RWB-E4-017 'Screen and states' (SCR-17, five states) and 'Endpoints' (two operations).
area: Contract and dispatch of the guarantor demand (S3, Guarantee)
owner_role: Solution architect with the rwb-guarantee tech lead and the rwb-comms owner
proposed: Publish the demand as the GuarantorNotice payload of the claim update operation on base /api/recovery/guarantee/v1 (DP-13), dispatch it as the workflow kit's Notify activity on the queue rwb-comms with one call per addressee, take the addressees from the case signal as party references, hold the template, the channel and the proof of delivery with rwb-comms, export the notice period as a parameter key, keep the clock as a durable Temporal timer inside GuaranteeClaimWorkflow, and record the notice facts that no column can hold on the local decision record (DP-03).

title: The notice payload, its required set, the approved-template answer, the delivery contract and the notice due date have no published shape
source: Ambiguity across FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3 A2.5 and 'Requirements served'; TSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v2 T3.1, T3.2, T4, T5.1, T5.3 and T-A.1; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 row R-GUA-06; Context pack S3 ownership rows; legacy RWB-E4-017 sections 7, 11, 15 and 19; Template and Rules v1 R3 and R5.5 DP-09 and DP-13
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC6; 8 Business rules; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.5; 12.7; 13 Solution plan; 15 Screens and states
description: One combined row for the notice contract. (1) No source publishes a notice payload: TSD S3 T3.1 gives the eight guarantee_claim fields and TSD S3 T-A.1 gives two claim operations with no request or response field list, so the properties of GuarantorNotice, their required set and their order are defined nowhere. (2) No source states the operation the notice rides: the legacy story's endpoint table lists the claim create and the claim update, TSD S3 T-A.1 API-S3-001 and API-S3-002 name the same two, and nothing states which of them carries the notice facts. (3) No source publishes the delivery contract. Architecture v5 slide 13 gives S3 a Temporal line to P6 and the workflow kit defines a generic Notify template with no business term in its interface, but no source names the activity, its queue, its input or its accepted and refused answers. (4) No source states the template rule's answer set: the notice types, the template codes, the reason codes of a refusal and the rule that decides what is current for a product are unnamed, and FSD S3 A2.5 says only 'the approved template'. (5) No source gives the notice due date a column, a field identifier or a parameter key, so the date the payload requires has no home in the model. (6) No source states the idempotency of the notice path or how a repeated demand within one notice cycle is deduped.
evidence: TSD S3 v2 T-A.1 (API-S3-001 POST and API-S3-002 PATCH, no notice operation) and T-A.2 (Request GuaranteeClaimRequest and GuaranteeClaimUpdate, Response GuaranteeClaim, no field list) and T3.1 (DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-022) and T3.2 (LOV-CLAIM-STATUS, LOV-CLAIM-TYPE only) and T5.3 ('None'); FSD S3 v3 A2.5.2 and 'Requirements served' REQ-S3-004 ('Guarantor and co-borrower notices are generated by rule and sent on the same path as customer notices'); Context pack S3 (topic rwb.guarantee.events.v1 with no event, workflow GuaranteeClaimWorkflow, two claim operations) and slide 13 row 'S3 Guarantee | P6 T E'; legacy RWB-E4-017 'Endpoints', 'Data' and 'Screen and states'.
owner_role: Solution architect with the rwb-guarantee tech lead and the rwb-comms owner
proposed: Publish GuarantorNotice with seven properties on the claim update operation of RWB-S3-E4013-CON, the approved-template rule with an accepted answer carrying the dispatch reference and a refused answer carrying the owner's reason code, the activity input on the queue rwb-comms, the exported notice-period key with the due-date rule, the record rule of DP-03, major version 1 with its fakes and a drift test, and record the payload's unnamed values as the working read of the assumption.
